cases.prompt:
Write the operator how-to for rotating the edge gateway TLS certificate from these notes. The security team will also read it when they audit a rotation.

# Notes: rotating the edge gateway TLS certificate

Collected from the platform team's chat and the old wiki page. Not yet a document.

- History: we used to rotate by hand with a shell script written in 2021, then moved to the `gwctl` tool in
  2024 after the script broke on the new appliance firmware; the old wiki page still describes the script and
  should not be used.
- Certs are valid 90 days. Rotation must happen at least 14 days before expiry, otherwise the monitoring raises a
  P2 alert and the on-call engineer gets paged.
- `gwctl cert status` shows days left. `gwctl cert request --csr` makes a CSR, which has to go to the internal CA
  through the PKI portal, and the CA usually takes one working day to sign it, sometimes up to three.
- Signed cert goes on the gateway with `gwctl cert install <file>`. That command validates the chain and refuses an
  incomplete one. It keeps the previous cert as a fallback for 7 days.
- `gwctl cert activate` switches traffic to the new cert. Active TLS sessions drop when that runs, so do it in the
  Tuesday 22:00-23:00 maintenance window unless there's an emergency.
- If clients fail after activation, `gwctl cert rollback` restores the previous cert, but only within those 7 days.
  After 7 days the fallback is deleted and cannot be restored.
- OCSP stapling has to be re-enabled after activation with `gwctl ocsp enable` because activation turns it off.
  Without it, some partner clients reject the connection.
- The security team audits each rotation afterwards: they need the CSR fingerprint and the activation time, which
  `gwctl cert log` prints. They do not run the procedure.
- Operators doing this are on the infra on-call rota; they know Linux and the gateway console but not PKI.
cases.behavior: Draft a how-to for a primary reader while serving a secondary one, applying the skill's own prose rules.
outcomes: Writes for the on-call operator first and serves the auditor's needs (CSR fingerprint, activation time from gwctl cert log) without reshaping the procedure around them.
Explains CSR, CA, and OCSP stapling at first use in plain terms.
Gives each procedural sentence one instruction within 20 words with any condition first, and keeps descriptive sentences within 25 words.
Places the signing lead time, the maintenance window, dropped sessions, and the 7-day rollback limit before the step each affects.
Uses headings that predict their content and keeps the history and the old script off the main path.
Keeps every number: 90 days, 14 days, one to three working days, 7 days, Tuesday 22:00-23:00; re-enabling OCSP is a step.
States what remains unverified and which evaluation the document received, without inventing procedure.

cases.prompt:
Review this documentation page and tell me what to fix.

# Information

## Overview

The backup subsystem, which was introduced as part of the storage modernization initiative and which leverages
the snapshot capabilities of the underlying ZFS pools in combination with the offsite replication service, is
designed to provide a robust and comprehensive solution for ensuring that customer data can be recovered in a
timely manner in the event of a failure.

## Details

Restores are performed via the `restorectl` utility; it requires the RPO-tier flag; it also needs the tenant ID;
the output goes to a staging dataset. Run `restorectl apply --tenant <id> --tier <tier>` if the staging dataset
has been verified. Snapshots are retained for 35 days for gold-tier tenants and 14 days for standard-tier tenants,
after which they are pruned by the retention daemon, which runs nightly at 02:00 UTC and cannot be paused while a
restore is in progress, so a restore of a snapshot older than 13 days on a standard-tier tenant can fail midway.

Historically restores were done by the storage team via tickets, which caused delays averaging 2.5 days, which is
why self-service was introduced in Q3.

Note: you must stop the tenant's application pods before running `restorectl apply`, otherwise the restore will
corrupt the live dataset.

## More

The RPO tier is determined by the tenant's SLA. ZFS send/recv is used under the hood with incremental streams
and the replication service uses mbuffer.
